question: Why do the Java and TypeScript targets differ on 51 production files, and are the targets structurally equivalent when both receive the production preprocessing boundary?
control: Experiment 013 cross-runtime conformance: TypeScript applied conditional-compilation preprocessing; the Java observation path received raw source.
candidate: Identical prepared source for both targets, plus a symbolic token-stream diagnosis that excludes token text and offsets.
selection: Complete frozen 1,244-file opaque production corpus and the 48-file public synthetic corpus.
acceptance: Record the first divergent symbolic token per differing file without publishing token text.
Group every difference by lexer rule and runtime behavior.
Provide a public reduced fixture for each reproducible class.
Correct the input-boundary defect when evidence supports it.
Rerun the complete cross-runtime structural gate.
